P1.q: Can this queue be used for a multi-node training job?
P1.expected: No. Never for multi-GPU or multi-node (no NVLink/InfiniBand).

P1.q: After warm-up, how much slower than A100 is it, and how strong is the evidence?
P1.expected: About 5% (approximate), from one measurement on a small fp32 CNN.

P1.q: What one-time cost should you expect?
According to the text, why is the queue mostly idle?
P1.expected: Stated as fact: the card is sm_120 and the envs' PyTorch ships kernels only to sm_90, so it runs via PTX JIT with nothing precompiled.

P1.q: Is it suitable for single-GPU work?

P2.q: Who receives a Slack message by default?
P2.expected: The user themself, as a DM.

P2.q: When may a message go to another person or channel?
P2.expected: Only when the user explicitly says "send to <person>" or "post in <channel>".

P2.q: In that case, may the agent send it immediately?
P2.expected: No. It must confirm with the user before sending.

P2.q: Does the rule cover drafts as well as sent messages?
P2.expected: Yes. Drafts also go to the user as a DM.

P3.q: What must you check before installing packages into an env?
P3.expected: bjobs: whether a cluster job using that env is still running.

P3.q: If a job is using the env, what are the options?
P3.expected: Wait for the job, or clone the env and install into the clone.

P3.q: Will code imported later in the live job definitely load the new package version?
P3.expected: Not definitely. It may load the new version.

P3.q: What must you do after any env change?
P3.expected: Immediately pip freeze to the pinned requirements file and note the date.

P4.q: When does the default Drive folder apply?
P4.expected: When an upload to Google Drive is requested for a pptx, docx, pdf, or html deliverable and no folder is given.

P4.q: What must you do before uploading?
P4.expected: List the folder and check for a file with the same name.

P4.q: May you overwrite an existing file with the same name?
P4.expected: Not someone else's file. The text does not say what to do about your own file.

P4.q: How should the files be copied?
P4.expected: Stage them in one local folder and rclone copy that folder once.

P4.q: How do you verify the upload, and what do you report?
P4.expected: rclone check --checksum --one-way; report the matching-file count; never --size-only.

P5.q: For which data must you ask before using Codex?
P5.expected: Patient data, embargoed collaborator data, or anything the user marked sensitive.

P5.q: Is it fine to send the user's own analyses?
What must you do before applying a Codex finding?
P5.expected: Open the cited file/line and confirm the finding.

P5.q: Does Codex's suggested wording always over-correct?
P5.expected: No. Sometimes, in one past review.

P5.q: How should an accepted fix be applied?
P5.expected: Keep the author's voice and make the minimum effective edit.
